title: Artin-Rees controls the A-adic stabilisation of the homology of a complex of finite modules over a Noetherian ring
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: This is a six-part structure theorem. Starting from a complex K -> L -> M of finite modules over a Noetherian ring A with H = Ker(beta)/Im(alpha), and the complexes induced modulo I^n with homology H_n, the lemma produces canonical maps H -> H_n and H_n -> H_{n-1} and then asserts that the pro-systems (H_n) and (H/I^n H) are isomorphic, that their limits agree, that (H_n) is Mittag-Leffler, and three further exactness statements (source lines 28866-28903). The proof must first rewrite H_n as beta^{-1}(I^n M)/(Im(alpha) + I^n L) and build the comparison maps from the inclusions beta^{-1}(I^n M) in beta^{-1}(I^{n-1} M) and Im(alpha) + I^n L in Im(alpha) + I^{n-1} L (proof lines 28906-28913). The genuinely non-routine part is then the construction of the map psi_n : H_n -> H/I^{n-c}H, which depends on two Artin-Rees constants c_1 and c_2 chosen so that beta^{-1}(I^n M) is contained in Ker(beta) + I^{n-c_1} L and Ker(beta) cap I^n L is contained in I^{n-c_2} Ker(beta) (proof lines 28916-28920), together with a well-definedness argument that tracks a second set of choices through those two containments (proof lines 28927-28941). Parts (1) to (6) are then derived, with (5) proved by summing over generators of I^c H_n (proof lines 28971-28978) and (6) by splitting into the two annihilation bounds, one from each Artin-Rees constant, which is why the single exponent c = c_1 + c_2 is what makes the statement true (proof lines 28981-28990).
